title: *args, **kwargs and keyword-only
summary: Flexible signatures, and how to call with unpacked collections.

steps.title: *args
body: A parameter written `*args` collects any extra **positional** arguments into a tuple, like C#'s `params`:
total(*values)     # 9: * at the call site spreads a list into arguments

steps.explain: `rest` is always a tuple, possibly empty. `*"abc"` spreads the string into three arguments.

steps.title: **kwargs
body: `**kwargs` collects extra **keyword** arguments into a dict:
parts = [f'{k}="{v}"' for k, v in attrs.items()]
tag("div", **options)            # ** spreads a dict into keyword arguments
The names `args` and `kwargs` are conventions; the stars do the work.

steps.explain: `**info` is a dict of every keyword argument. `**settings` at the call site spreads a dict back into keywords.

steps.title: Keyword-only and positional-only
body: Anything after a bare `*` must be passed **by name**. Anything before a `/` must be passed by position:
Keyword-only flags make call sites readable: `sort(items, reverse=True)` instead of a mystery `True`. This is why `sorted(xs, key=...)` cannot be called as `sorted(xs, len)`.

steps.prompt: Given `def f(a, b=2, *args, c, **kw)`, which call raises `TypeError`?
steps.explain: `c` comes after `*args`, so it is keyword-only and has no default: every call must name it.

steps.prompt: For `def f(a, /, b, *, c)`, how must each parameter be passed?
Complete the signature so `report("Q1", 10, 20, 30, sep="; ")` works.
code: return title + ": " + sep.join(str(v) for v in values)
steps.explain: After `*values`, every remaining parameter (like `sep`) is keyword-only automatically.

steps.title: Format a record
prompt: - the name, then if there are tags, ` [` + tags joined by `sep` + `]`
- then each field in **alphabetical** order as ` key=value`
record("bo", "x", sep="|", age=30, city="Oslo")  # 'bo [x] age=30 city=Oslo'
template: Dojo.eq("fields sorted", "bo [x] age=30 city=Oslo", record("bo", "x", city="Oslo", age=30))
Dojo.eq("spread a list and a dict", "cy [p, q] z=1", record("cy", *["p", "q"], **{"z": 1}))
